dhp383:1: Strive and cut off the stream, remove desire, brahmin,
dhp383:3: knowing the destruction of the conditioned, be one who knows that which is not made, brahmin.
dhp384:1: When a brahmin has, through two things, crossed over,
dhp384:4: then, for one who knows, all the fetters are laid to rest.
dhp385:2: For whom the near shore, the far shore or both do not exist,
dhp385:3: free of anxiety, being detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp386:1: The meditator sitting down, the one who is dustless, who has done his duty, without pollutants,
dhp386:4: who has reached the ultimate good, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp387:1: The sun is radiant by day, the moon shines by night,
dhp387:3: the accoutred noble is radiant, the meditating brahmin is radiant,
dhp387:5: yet every day and night the Buddha is radiant through his power.
dhp388:1: Warding off wickedness one is called a brahmin,
dhp388:2: one living austerely is said to be an ascetic,
dhp388:3: * because of driving forth (all) stain from oneself
dhp388:4: one is said to be one who has gone forth.
dhp389:1: A brahmin should not hit a brahmin, nor should he abandon him,
dhp389:3: woe to the one who strikes a brahmin, further: woe to the one who abandons him.
dhp390:1: It is no little good for the brahmin:
dhp390:2: when the mind is held back from what is dear,
dhp390:3: whenever his mind turns back from violence,
dhp390:4: then there is a calming of suffering.
dhp391:1: For whom there is no wrong-doing bodily, verbally or mentally,
dhp391:4: being restrained in (these) three things, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp392:1: That one from whom one learned Dhamma taught by the Perfect Sambuddha,
dhp392:3: with respect bow down to him, like brahmin (bows) at fire-sacrifice.
dhp393:2: Not because of matted hair, family or birth is one a true brahmin,
dhp393:3: in whom there is truth and Dhamma, that one is pure, that one is surely a brahmin.
dhp394:1: Why do you have your hair matted, stupid one, and why your deer-skin?
dhp394:3: Within you there is a jungle, you (only) polish the outside.
dhp395:1: That one who wears discarded clothes, who is lean with protruding veins,
dhp395:3: who meditates alone in the forest, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp396:2: I do not call one a brahmin simply because of being born from a (certain) womb,
dhp396:4: that one is just one who says ‘bho’ if he is attached;
dhp396:6: having nothing and unattached, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp397:1: Whoever has cut off all the fetters surely does not tremble,
dhp397:3: surmounting attachments, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp398:1: (Whoever) has cut off the thong, the strap, the rope, together with the bridle,
dhp398:3: who has thrown off the obstacle and is awakened, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp399:1: Whoever, being pure, forbears with punishment, bondage and abuse,
dhp399:4: having the strength of endurance, having an army of strengths,, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp400:1: (Whoever is) controlled of mind, dutiful, virtuous, taint-free,
dhp400:4: well-trained and in his last body, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp401:1: Like water on the lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on a needle,
dhp401:4: he who is unsmeared by desires, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp402:1: Whoever knows right here the destruction of his suffering,
dhp402:3: putting down the burden, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp403:1: The deeply wise sagacious one, skilled in what is path and not path,
dhp403:4: who has reached the ultimate good, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp404:1: (Whoever) doesn’t mix with either householders or the houseless,
dhp404:4: wandering homeless, with few desires, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp405:1: * Whoever has laid down the stick (used) against fearful and fearless beings,
dhp405:4: who neither hurts nor kills, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp406:2: Being friendly with the hostile, calm amongst those holding a stick,
dhp406:4: not attached amongst those attached, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp407:2: Whoever has dropped off passion and hatred, conceit and anger,
dhp407:4: like a mustard seed from a needle, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp408:1: (Whoever) speaks a word of truth that is informed and is not coarse,
dhp408:4: through which no one would be angry, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp409:1: * Whoever in the world does not take what is not given, long, short,
dhp409:4: small, large, attractive or unattractive, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp410:1: For the one who has no longings in this world or in the next world,
dhp410:4: being without longings, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp411:1: For the one who has no desires, who, through knowledge, is without doubt,
dhp411:4: who has reached immersion in the deathless, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp412:1: Whoever here has overcome clinging to both merit and demerit,
dhp412:4: who is griefless, dustless and pure, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp413:1: (Whoever) just like the moon is stainless, pure, clear and undisturbed,
dhp413:3: has destroyed joy in existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp414:1: He who has crossed the difficult and dangerous path through births and deaths and delusion,
dhp414:4: the meditator who has crossed over to the further shore, free of lust and free of doubt,
dhp414:6: unattached and cooled down, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp415:2: Whoever, giving up sensual desires, would wander homeless here,
dhp415:4: destroying desires and existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp416:1: Whoever, giving up craving, would wander homeless here,
dhp416:3: destroying craving and existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp417:1: Abandoning the human yoke, overcoming the divine yoke,
dhp417:4: being unattached to all yokes, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp418:2: Abandoning delight and aversion, cooled off and free from cleaving,
dhp418:3: a hero who vanquished the whole world, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp419:1: Whoever knows in every way beings’ passing and their rebirth,
dhp419:3: unattached, fortunate, awake, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp420:1: For the one whose destiny is unknown to gods, gandhabbas and men –
dhp420:4: being pollutant-free, an Arahat, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp421:2: For whom there is nothing in the past, the future or the present,
dhp421:4: having nothing and unattached, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp422:1: A noble leader, heroic, a great seer, victorious,
dhp422:3: free of lust, cleansed and awakened, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp423:2: Whoever knows their former lives, and sees heaven and the downfall,
dhp423:3: and has attained birth’s destruction, the sage, accomplished in deep knowledge,
dhp423:6: who is accomplished in all accomplishments, that one I say is a brahmin.
dhp423:7: The Chapter about Brahmins, the Twenty-Sixth
